newsitem.title: FRANCE: Remy shares weak in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Remy shares weak in late trade.

text.p: Shares in Remy-Cointreau fell in late trading on Tuesday after the drinks group issued results that stirred doubts about its prospects for earnings growth and debt reduction, analysts said.
The stock, which rose in early trading, was down 1.70 francs, or 1.24 percent, at 135.30 francs at 1520 GMT. The bourse's CAC index was down 0.5 percent.
"The operating results aren't improving, and their debt is growing," said one analyst.
Remy earlier reported its operating result fell three percent to 210 million francs in the first half to September 30.
Company officials told a news conference that the group's debt rose to over seven billion francs in the first half from over six billion at the end of the 1995/96 year ended on March 31.
Another analyst said the operating result was slightly lower than anticipated. "And it compares with a poor result a year earlier," she said.

Remy reported an 81 percent drop in 1996/97 first-half pre-tax attributable profit after recording lower exceptional gains related to a prior debt restructuring -- 44 million francs in the first half, compared with 257 million a year ago.
Its pre-tax, pre-exceptional loss narrowed to one million francs from a year-earlier loss of 39 million francs.
"Even if they show mechanical improvements, they haven't arrived at reducing their debt. And it's not clear how the margin will evolve," the analyst said.
Remy officials said they were studying asset sales to reduce debt but added they were not in a hurry as they sought the best price.
